title: Composition of regular ring maps
statement: Let $A\to B$ and $B\to C$ be regular ring maps [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] of commutative rings. If for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset A$ the fibre ring $C\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] of the composite $A\to C$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], then the composite $A\to C$ is a regular ring map.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07QI (more-algebra-lemma-regular-composition, line 10440); its proof uses Lemma 07C1 (lemma-regular-base-change) and algebra.tex lemma-flat-over-regular-with-regular-fibre, 'some details omitted'

proof.text: Fix $\mathfrak p\subset A$ and a finite purely inseparable extension $k/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. First localize at $\mathfrak p$: flatness localizes, and the fibre of $A_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\mathfrak p}$ is the localization of the corresponding fibre of $A\to B$, so the Noetherian and geometrically regular fibre conditions are unchanged. Precisely: $B_{\mathfrak p}=B\otimes_AA_{\mathfrak p}$ is flat over $A_{\mathfrak p}$ by flat base change [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change], and for a prime $\mathfrak p'A_{\mathfrak p}$ of $A_{\mathfrak p}$ the fibre $B_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak p}}\kappa(\mathfrak p')=B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ is the fibre of $A\to B$ over $\mathfrak p'$, Noetherian and geometrically regular; so $A_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular by [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. The quotient $A_{\mathfrak p}\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is a finite-type map, so [lem-weil-pbc-regular-base-change] gives a regular map $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to B_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak p}}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. The finite extension $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to k$ is again finite type, and a second application gives a regular map $k\to B_k:=B\otimes_A k$. Since the base is a field, $B_k$ is Noetherian and regular (take the trivial purely inseparable extension in the definition). The hypothesis says $C\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is Noetherian; since $k/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is finite, $C_k:=C\otimes_A k$ is a finite-type algebra over that fibre and is therefore Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian].

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07QI, lines 10446--10450, with localization made explicit via Lemma 07C0 and two finite-type applications of Lemma 07C1

proof.text: The map $B_k\to C_k$ is flat by flat base change [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change]. Let $\mathfrak q'\subset B_k$ lie over $\mathfrak q\subset B$ and write $K=\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ and $K'=\kappa(\mathfrak q')$. The map $B_{\mathfrak p}\to B_k$ is of finite type, so $K'/K$ is finitely generated by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-residue-field-extension-finitely-generated]. Its fibre is the tensor base change $F_{\mathfrak q'}=(C\otimes_B K)\otimes_K K'$. The ring $C\otimes_B K$ is Noetherian and geometrically regular over $K$ because $B\to C$ is regular. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-regular-finitely-generated-extensions] to every finite purely inseparable extension of $K'$ (each remains finitely generated over $K$) shows that $F_{\mathfrak q'}$ is Noetherian and geometrically regular over $K'$. Independently, its Noetherianity is also visible directly: $F_{\mathfrak q'}$ is a localization of a quotient of the Noetherian ring $C_k$ from Step 1, using the fibre localization/quotient description [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian].

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07QI, lines 10450--10452; geometric regularity after field extension is Algebra Lemma 0381 (captured by the cited finitely-generated-extension node), and fibre localization is the 07BZ fibre formula

proof.text: For every prime $\mathfrak r\subset C_k$, let $\mathfrak q'=\mathfrak r\cap B_k$. The local map $(B_k)_{\mathfrak q'}\to(C_k)_{\mathfrak r}$ is flat, its source is regular by Step 1, and its closed fibre is a localization of $F_{\mathfrak q'}$, hence regular by Step 2. Apply the public local criterion [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-regular-with-regular-fibre] (Algebra Tag 031E) to conclude that $(C_k)_{\mathfrak r}$ is regular local. Since the Noetherianity here is that of $C_k=C\otimes_A k$ established in Step 1 (not of $C$ itself), every localization of the Noetherian ring $C_k$ is regular local, so $C_k$ is regular. As this holds for every $\mathfrak p$ and every finite purely inseparable $k/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, the fibres of $A\to C$ are geometrically regular; flatness of $A\to C$ follows from [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-comp], and [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] gives that $A\to C$ is regular.
